_note: Recurring-series programming for Film Day at School (channels/publish.php), replacing the channel's original one-off ia-import 'balanced' bin-packed schedule.json with the standard architecture (see docs/guide-update.md and the RetroVision precedent, channels/retrovision/programming.json). All 167 real Internet Archive items from catalog.json were re-curated by actual subject matter (see series/film-day-*/series.json) into ten thematic series -- Safety First, Health Class, Mind Your Manners, Marriage & the Office, Civics Hour, Science Shorts, Wired World, The Working World, On the Move, and Shorts & Curiosities -- each a themed 'class period', nine of twelve blocks a full 2 hours. The two largest episode pools (The Working World, 31 episodes, 24,007s total; Mind Your Manners, 21 episodes, 16,244s total) each air twice daily in independent AM/PM blocks -- but same-duration AM/PM blocks of one series advance in lockstep and replay the IDENTICAL lineup every day (same bug Maker Channel's own _note already warns about and avoids): each pair's PM block is deliberately a different length (5400s vs. the AM block's 7200s) so the two consume their shared pool at different rates and actually drift apart, the same technique Maker already uses. Shorts & Curiosities' pool is only 7 episodes/4,899s total -- far short of a 2-hour slot -- so its block is also 5400s, not 7200s; all three shortened blocks leave a genuine, intentional gap (station break) between their own real content and the next fixed-time block, rather than silently padding out 2-hour slots they can't actually fill or mislabeling true dead air as program content. Every block opts into multi-episode packing (packing.enabled, mode sequential, on_unfit defer) so a slot plays as many complete, approved short films back-to-back as actually fit -- these are archival films/shorts (20s-3284s), not hour-long shows. boundary.mode is hard on every block: the longest single approved episode in any theme is 3284s (The Middleton Family at the New York World's Fair, in Civics Hour), comfortably under even the shortened 5400s slots, so no block has ever actually needed to run over.

blocks.title: Health Class
blocks.description: Personal hygiene, nutrition, disease prevention, and mental-health instruction from the Internet Archive's Prelinger Archives -- the classroom health unit, decade by decade, from germ theory to "keeping mentally fit."

blocks.title: Civics Hour
blocks.description: American history, government, and civic life from the Internet Archive's Prelinger Archives -- the Bill of Rights, Congress, World's Fairs, wartime homefront propaganda, and the project of building postwar America.

blocks.title: Science Shorts
blocks.description: Natural science and classroom physics from the Internet Archive's Prelinger Archives -- sound, light, color, electricity, and the small creatures (and smaller atoms) a mid-century science class might cover.

blocks.title: The Working World
blocks.description: Vocational-guidance and industrial-process films from the Internet Archive's Prelinger Archives -- trades, careers, factories, and the consumer economics of banking, money, and meat, as taught to generations of American students.

blocks.title: Mind Your Manners
blocks.description: Teenage social-guidance films from the Internet Archive's Prelinger Archives: dating, grooming, popularity, honesty, and the agony of adolescence as mid-century classroom-film producers imagined it.

blocks.title: Safety First
blocks.description: Civil-defense drills, "scared straight" crime dramas, and workplace/traffic safety shorts from the Internet Archive's Prelinger Archives -- duck-and-cover atomic preparedness, juvenile-delinquency cautionary tales, and everyday hazard-avoidance films shown to generations of American schoolchildren.

blocks.title: Wired World
blocks.description: Telephone, radio, television, and the first computers, from the Internet Archive's Prelinger Archives -- how 20th-century America talked, broadcast, and began to compute.

blocks.title: On the Move
blocks.description: Roads, railroads, airports, and the infrastructure of getting around, from the Internet Archive's Prelinger Archives -- mid-century America in transit.

blocks.title: Marriage & the Office
blocks.description: Social-guidance films for grown-ups from the Internet Archive's Prelinger Archives -- marriage, housework, office etiquette, and the workplace politics of mid-century American domestic and clerical life.

blocks.title: Shorts & Curiosities
blocks.description: Newsreels, novelty shorts, and one-of-a-kind oddities from the Internet Archive's Prelinger Archives -- too short or too strange to fit any other period on the schedule.
